title: Adaptive Operator Selection Surface (AOSS) for heterogeneous GPU inference
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Problem: Our current kernel-picking policy is a small rule-based table keyed by (model, stage=prefill|decode, seqlen-bucket). It yields good median latency but shows cost inefficiencies and 99th-percentile tail regressions on mixed workloads and across GPU generations. Goal: build an Adaptive Operator Selection Surface (AOSS) that replaces the static table with a compact learned/profiled surface that maps observable request features to a ranked set of operator/kernel candidates with confidence scores, plus a safe fallback. AOSS should be architecture- and seqlen-aware, support warm-start from offline microbenchmarks, and allow controlled online exploration.
acceptance_criteria: 1) New policy reduces per-token cost by >=8% on mixed chat+completion benchmark vs current table under identical throughput. 2) 99th-percentile latency regression <=5% vs baseline on production-like tail workload. 3) Runtime supports per-request kernel ranking and safe immediate fallback. 4) Canary rollout automation (1%->25%->100%) with automatic rollback on latency/cost regression alerts. 5) Offline profile artifacts stored in artifact store with reproducible runner.
design_decisions: - Surface input features: model_id, layer_count, vocabulary size, stage (prefill/decode), request_seq_len, response_seq_len_hint, batch_size (effective), GPU_arch, free_mem_ratio, observed occupancy. - Representation: bucketized continuous features + one-hot categorical -> small feature vector. - Core: use per-arch cost surfaces built from offline microbenchmarks (latency, throughput, memory) with lightweight isotonic smoothing across seqlen. - Online layer: contextual bandit with Thompson sampling for controlled probes: schedule low-frequency probes under capacity headroom using shadow or probe tokens. - Fallback: safe kernel per-model that prioritizes deterministic latency and correctness; always available. - Warm-start: seed bandit priors from offline profile means and variances. - Storage: store profiles by (arch, model_family, quantization_profile) in artifact service; profile version pinned in rollout. - Safety: probes must respect latency SLO budget; abort probing when tail exceeds thresholds. - Observability: expose per-kernel counters and cost/latency heatmaps in console; allow manual pinning to table for debugging.
implementation_notes: - Offline profiler: extend existing microbench harness to sweep attention kernel variants, unroll factors, and memory layouts for prefill vs decode paths. Save results as CSV + small index. - Runtime integration: add AOSS policy module behind kernel-advisor interface; keep old table as fallback and toggle via feature flag. - Probing: implement token-level shadow probes that run at lower priority on spare capacity GPUs; fallback to synthetic microbench when no spare capacity. - Rollout: implement canary control in orchestration layer: route 1% of traffic to AOSS-pass, compare metrics. - Tests: unit for ranking logic, integration with model-serving e2e, soak test for 24h on staging. - Metrics: per-candidate latency P50/P95/P99, cost-per-token estimate, probe success/failure, revert count. - Performance budget: additional CPU <5% per runtime process, memory delta <50MB.
tasks: Extend microbench harness to profile attention kernels across seqlen and batch sizes
Design compact on-disk profile format and storage keying
Implement AOSS policy module and feature flag
Implement controlled probe scheduler with SLO-aware throttling
Integrate metric exports and Console heatmap for operator surfaces
Create canary runbook and automation for ramp/rollback
Add e2e regression tests and staging soak
